L183:                                                 PRODUCTIVITY AND COSTS
L184:                                             Third Quarter 2026, Preliminary
L185: 
L186:     Nonfarm business sector labor productivity increased 3.6 percent in the third quarter of 2026, the
L187:     U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today, as output increased 3.7 percent and hours worked
L188:     increased 0.1 percent. (All quarterly percent changes in this release are seasonally adjusted annualized
L189:     rates.) From the same quarter a year ago, nonfarm business sector labor productivity increased 2.1
L190:     percent in the third quarter of 2026. (See table A1.)
L191: 
L192:     Unit labor costs in the nonfarm business sector decreased 0.7 percent in the third quarter of 2026,
L193:     reflecting a 2.9-percent increase in hourly compensation and a 3.6-percent increase in productivity. Unit
L194:     labor costs increased 2.4 percent over the last four quarters. (See tables A1 and 2.)
L195:     BLS calculates unit labor costs as the ratio of hourly compensation to labor productivity. Increases in
L196:     hourly compensation tend to increase unit labor costs and increases in productivity tend to reduce them.
L197:

L788: ORLANDO, Florida, Nov 5 (Reuters) - US stocks plunged on Thursday, led by a ferocious selloff in tech and AI-related stocks as investors reassessed implications for the AI data center buildout from the Democrats' sweeping wins in this week's midterm elections. Chip stocks posted their second-biggest fall on record, and interest rates traders pushed back the expected timing of the Federal Reserve's next rate hike to March.
